headline: High-risk workspace-to-runtime bridge: Notion AI can feed OpenHands sensitive content, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI ingests workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while OpenHands can use MCP, browsers, and shell actions. If Notion content is copied or synced into OpenHands, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use. The bridge is not default-proven, so I rate it medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Notion page content is transferred into OpenHands prompts or files
IF OpenHands treats imported text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Paste only sanitized excerpts into OpenHands
Add a fixed instruction prefix that ignores embedded commands
Review Notion content for untrusted markup before transfer
Use a separate scratch page for agent handoff
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between workspace and runtime

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, and OpenHands reads and writes files in a runtime sandbox with broad egress. If the same sensitive material is moved between them, OpenHands can expose it to a model provider or MCP server. The shared-data path is plausible, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF workspace pages containing sensitive data are copied into the OpenHands runtime
IF OpenHands sends runtime context to a configured model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Keep sensitive pages out of the runtime mount
Redact secrets before handoff
Disable unnecessary MCP servers
Use a dedicated low-sensitivity workspace for agent collaboration
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances, and OpenHands can write files in a mounted runtime volume. If both operate on the same shared artifact, concurrent edits can overwrite each other. The profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces, but not unrestricted same-dir writes, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same workspace artifact or mounted file
IF no external locking or merge step is used
mitigations: Assign one agent as read-only reviewer
Use separate working copies
Manually reconcile diffs before saving
Avoid simultaneous edits to the same page or file
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and OpenHands runs an agent loop with shell, browser, and editor actions. If OpenHands treats Notion output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code or runtime actions. The pathway exists in default workflows, but verification can interrupt it.
conditions: IF OpenHands uses Notion-generated text as the basis for code or operational actions
IF no human or automated verification step checks the output
mitigations: Require a second-pass review before execution
Mark Notion output as untrusted input
Ask OpenHands to cite source pages before acting
Limit OpenHands to drafting, not executing, on first pass
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI processes workspace pages under the invoking user's Notion permissions, while OpenHands handles files in a runtime sandbox and can send context to a user-configured model provider. If regulated data is moved from Notion into OpenHands, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data from Notion is transferred into OpenHands
IF the configured model provider or MCP server has different retention or residency terms
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of OpenHands
Use a provider with matching compliance terms
Document retention expectations before transfer
Delete temporary runtime files after use
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls
